(54) Title: PROCESS FOR THE PREPARATION OF 9-[(2-HYDROXYETHOXY)METHYL]GUANINE

(57) Abstract

There is described a process for the preparation of acyclovir by hydrolysis of N2-acetyl-9-(2-acetoxyethoxymethyl)guanine with monoethanolamine and isolation of acyclovir by neutralization with an acid and filtration. There is furthermore described a method for the purification of acyclovir by transformation of it into one of its alkali metal salts and neutralization of the alkali metal salt thus obtained.

PROCESS FOR THE PREPARATION OF 9-[(2-HYDROXYETHOXY)METHYL]GUANINE

The present invention relates to a process for the preparation of 9-[(2-hydroxyethoxy)methyl] guanine, known under its International Non-proprietary Name "acyclovir", hereinbelow designated by this name and represented by the following structural formula I

(structure: OH on purine ring; H2N–C; N; N; CH2OCH2CH2OH)  (I)

Acyclovir has been disclosed for the first time in Belgian patent 833,006; in this document there are also described various processes for its preparation, including the process involving the final step of transformation of the O-protected acyclovir into acyclovir. The expression "O-protected acyclovir" designates the protected acyclovir on the aliphatic hydroxy group. According to this method, the O-protecting group is, in general, an ester, more particularly an acyl group, preferably a benzoyl group. Removal of the O-protecting group is carried out, according to BE 833,006, by treatment with ammonia saturated methanol to give acyclovir in a 75% yield.

Other methods for the preparation of acyclovir are indicated by the literature. Thus, EP 532,878 discloses the preparation of O,N2-diprotected acyclovir by acetylation and subsequent deprotection by treatment with sodium hydroxyde to give acyclovir in a 92% yield. According to this document, however, diacetylacyclovir [N2-acetyl-9-(2-acetoxyethoxymethyl)guanine] is in its turn obtained in admixture with N2-acetyl-7-(2-acetoxyethoxymethyl)guanine in the 2.5:1 ratio which requires a previous chromatographic separation of the two isomers.

Thus, according to one of its aspects, the present invention concerns a process for the preparation of acyclovir which comprises

(a) treating the N2-acetyl-9-(2-acetoxyethoxymethyl)guanine (diacetylacyclovir) with an alcanolamine in aqueous solution;

(b) isolating the acyclovir thus obtained by treatment with a mineral or organic acid and subsequently filtering the separated precipitate.

In the preferred realization form, step (a) is carried out with monoethanolamine.

Step (a) is carried out starting from a N2-acetyl-9-(2-acetoxy ethoxymethyl)guanine which may be pure or in a wet state by the residual solvent of its synthesis, in aqueous medium at a temperature of 70÷95°C. At this temperature the reaction is complete after about 3 hours.

Among the alcanolamines, monoethanolamine is preferred but appreciable results are obtained also using diethanolamine and triethanolamine, even though with longer reaction times.

In step (b), after the possible removal of the residual solvent, for example by distillation under vacuum, the reaction mixture is treated with an acid, for example with acetic acid, up to neutrality. Acyclovir thus obtained is isolated by filtration and subsequent washing with an appropriate solvent, for example a ketone such as acetone, methylethylketone or methylisobutylketone, and final drying.

In general, the product obtained is of great purity, read for use in pharmaceutical formulations.

If a further increase of the purity degree or if an acyclovir obtained by another route is available, the product may be, in general, purified by transformation in one of its alkali metal salts, preferably in its sodium salt and subsequent neutralization in aqueous medium. Such a purification presents the advantage that it can be carried out on any crude acyclovir obtained according to any other method.

route.title: PROCESS FOR THE PREPARATION OF 9-[(2-HYDROXYETHOXY)METHYL]GUANINE (ACYCLOVIR)

steps.step_label: Example 1 — hydrolysis/deprotection of diacetylacyclovir with monoethanolamine and isolation (steps a–b)

products.name: acyclovir (wet of acetone)
products.amount: 50 g wet, corresponding to 33.250 g dry

conditions.temperature: heated at 90 °C; cooled to 60 °C for acid addition; further cooled to about 20 °C
conditions.other: pH 6.8–7.2 after 80% acetic acid addition; then 60 ml water and 60 ml acetone added; crystalline product filtered and washed with acetone

steps.notes: Product has purity characteristics corresponding to those of a USP standard; general process taught at 70–95 °C, ~3 h; alcanolamine may be mono-, di- or triethanolamine (monoethanolamine preferred)
steps.evidence: A mixture of 46.250 g (0.149 moles) of N2-acetyl-9-(2-acetoxyethoxymethyl)guanine and 32.750 g (0.536 moles) of monoethanolamine in 600 ml of deionized water are heated at 90°C for 3 hours ... Thus, there is obtained 50 g of acyclovir, wet of acetone ... Yield: 98.7% of the theoretical.

steps.step_label: Example 2(a) — formation of acyclovir sodium salt (step c)

reactants.name: acyclovir, wet of acetone (from Example 1)
reactants.amount: 30 g wet, corresponding to 19.950 g dry product

solvents.name: acetone
solvents.amount: 37.5 ml then 195 ml (plus 1.5 ml wash and 35 ml wash)

products.name: acyclovir sodium salt (wet of acetone)
products.amount: 25.5 g wet, corresponding to 23.2 g dry product

conditions.temperature: solution heated to 35 °C; suspension cooled to 15 °C
conditions.other: pH 11.8–12.0 after NaOH; charcoal treatment then filtration washing with 1.5 ml deionized water and 1.5 ml acetone; precipitation by adding 195 ml acetone; product washed with 35 ml acetone

steps.notes: Sodium salt used as such (wet) in the subsequent neutralization step
steps.evidence: To a mixture of 30 g of acyclovir, wet of acetone, obtained according to Example 1 ... 36 ml of deionized water and 9 ml of 30% sodium hydroxide are added in order to have a pH of 11.8 ÷ 12.0 ... There is obtained 25.5 g of sodium salt, wet of acetone, corresponding to 23.2 g of dry product.

steps.step_label: Example 2(b) — neutralization of sodium salt to purified acyclovir (step d)

reactants.name: acyclovir sodium salt, wet of acetone (from Example 2a)
reactants.amount: 24 g wet, corresponding to 21.9 g dry product

conditions.temperature: cooled at 15 °C; dried under vacuum at 80 °C
conditions.other: filtered, washed with 35 ml deionized water and 35 ml acetone; dried to residual moisture not higher than 5%

steps.evidence: To a solution of 24 g of acyclovir sodium salt, wet of acetone ... in 220 ml of deionized water, 6.75 ml of 80% acetic acid are added ... there is obtained 18.2 g of acyclovir having a purity of 99.85%.

steps.step_label: Example 3 — repeat of Example 1 at smaller scale with drying

products.name: acyclovir
products.amount: 18.9 g wet of acetone; 12.650 g after drying

conditions.temperature: as Example 1 (90 °C); drying under vacuum at 80 °C
conditions.other: By operating as described in Example 1

steps.evidence: By operating as described in Example 1, from 17.5 g of N2-acetyl-9-(2-acetoxyethoxymethyl)guanine 18.9 g of acyclovir, wet of acetone, are obtained ... 12.650 g of acyclovir with a purity of 99.25% are obtained.

steps.step_label: Example 4 — purification of crude acyclovir from another route via sodium salt (steps c–d)

reactants.name: acyclovir, purity 95.47% (prepared according to Example 6 of BE 833,006)

conditions.other: By operating as described in Example 2; neutralization of the sodium salt in aqueous solution using 80% acetic acid

steps.evidence: By operating as described in Example 2, starting from 4.750 g of acyclovir with a purity of 95.47% ... 5.08 g of sodium salt are obtained. By neutralization ... using 80% acetic acid, 4.220 g of acyclovir with a purity of 99.27% are obtained.

conditions.other: hydrolysis with an aqueous solution of an alcanolamine, preferably monoethanolamine

steps.evidence: hydrolysis with an aqueous solution of an alcanolamine, preferably monoethanolamine
